nv_alternative_crag.blurb: A small sport crag in the Ash Spring part of Calico Basin, Red Rock. Eleven bolted lines, nearly all in the 5.12 range, with a single 5.11 and a single 5.13, so this is a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. The sandstone walls look northeast and northwest and sit in shade almost all day in midwinter; in spring the left side catches some early light and the right side loses the sun by late afternoon. Wind is common. Few routes start independently, so a handful of parties makes it feel crowded. The climb up to it is steep and takes roughly half an hour, and a flat ledge at the base gives you somewhere to rest.

nv_brevity_wall.blurb: A short limestone sport wall in the Mormon Mountains of southern Nevada, a remote, lightly developed range where you can go days without meeting anyone. Eleven bolted routes, all between 5.11 and 5.12, with more of them at the harder end. The rock is mostly vertical and pocketed, with crimps and water-carved runnels. The wall faces north and stays shaded all day, which helps in warm spells, though the range is windy and high summer can be too hot. Spring and autumn are the comfortable seasons. The way in is a wash walk of roughly twenty minutes after a long dirt road from the interstate.

nv_the_pearl_climbs.blurb: A cluster of eleven sandstone boulder problems within the Kraft Boulders in Red Rock, close to the main trail and a short walk from the lot. Most problems are easy to moderate: six sit at V0 or V1, with a scattering of middle grades and a few hard ones reaching V6. The main boulder is good-sized with a smooth southeast face that gets sun until mid-afternoon, while the northeast side sees little sun. A busy, sociable spot, with a well-known problem that sits right beside the path. Bring pads and keep off the rock when it is damp.

nv_strawberry_hill_buttress.blurb: A buttress of sandstone up First Creek Canyon in Red Rock, above the First Creek Slabs and recognizable by its rose-coloured upper section. Eleven trad lines run from 5.6 to 5.10, with most in the 5.7 to 5.9 band, and the longer ones go four or five pitches, which makes it a good pick for moderate multi-pitch. It is made of a slabby eastern part and a western part where the main descent lies, involving a short scramble and a few rappels. Expect a trail walk of around 45 minutes to get there.

nv_solar_slab_upper_tier.blurb: The upper tier of the Solar Slab buttress near the mouth of Oak Creek Canyon in Red Rock. Ten sandstone trad routes, mostly between 5.6 and 5.9, ranging from a couple of pitches to a dozen, with airy climbing throughout. The lines begin several hundred feet off the ground, so you reach them by climbing a lower-tier route first, and they all end on a roomy shoulder at the top of the buttress. Getting down means rappelling with two ropes or taking one of the walk-off gullies, some of which are very exposed. It suits parties comfortable with long days on moderate ground.

nv_rose_tower.blurb: A compact sandstone tower on the lower eastern slopes of Juniper Peak, reached through the Juniper Canyon approach in Red Rock. Ten routes, nearly all trad, running from 5.6 to 5.10, with the bulk around 5.7 and a few harder lines in the 5.10 range. The moderate classic here is popular and long, and multi-pitch lines make up much of the appeal. Descent is by a steep gully on the north side of the tower, which does not return to the base, so take everything with you. The area has a waste problem, so pack out your own.
